text.p: Dollar-sensitive retailer Delhaize led the Bel-20 index of leading shares to record highs in generally quiet early business, with dealers saying the 2,100-point resistance level would be no major obstacle.
At 0930 GMT, the Bel-20 was up 10.83 points, or 0.52 percent at 2,098.46 after touching an intra-day record of 2,099.44 minutes earlier.
"If there is no resistance for the dollar and interest rates, why should there be resistance for the Bel-20?" said Gert De Mesure at Delen Bank.
Delhaize, already the biggest gainer on Wednesday with a 2.26 percent rise, was up 1.5 percent at 2,065 francs with a high 30,945 shares traded.
"Delhaize is up, despite (its U.S. unit) Food Lion which has been slipping over the past three weeks. It's still the higher dollar which supports them," said De Mesure.
